title: WHO Guidelines for Essential Trauma Care & Basic Life Support
authority: World Health Organization & American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma
statutory_shield: Protection of Good Samaritans under Section 134A of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019

protocols.protocol_name: WHO Stop The Bleed & Severe Trauma Hemorrhage Control
protocols.section: Guideline 4.1: Direct Pressure, Wound Packing & Arterial Tourniquet Protocol

steps.title: Apply Firm Continuous Direct Pressure
steps.action_instruction: Cover the bleeding wound immediately with clean gauze, cloth, or bare gloved hands. Push down directly and hard on the bleeding vessel without lifting to check.
steps.warning_note: Do not release pressure or remove soaked dressings; layer additional cloths on top.

steps.title: Pack Deep Cavity Wounds (Junctional Hemorrhage)
steps.action_instruction: For deep wounds in groin, armpit, or neck, tightly pack hemostatic gauze or clean cloth directly into the wound cavity until full, then hold firm continuous pressure for at least 3 minutes.
steps.warning_note: Do not pack wounds inside chest or abdomen; apply flat direct pressure only.

steps.title: Deploy Arterial Tourniquet for Extremity Bleeding
steps.action_instruction: If bleeding from an arm or leg does not stop with direct pressure or is spurting bright red blood, place an arterial tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound (never over a joint). Tighten the windlass until bleeding stops completely.
steps.warning_note: Record the exact application time on the tourniquet. Never loosen or remove a tourniquet once applied; only hospital surgeons may release it.

steps.title: Prevent Hypothermia and Elevate Extremity
steps.action_instruction: Keep the victim warm with a thermal blanket or dry jackets. If bone is not fractured, gently elevate the bleeding limb above heart level.
steps.warning_note: Trauma victims with hypothermia lose blood clotting ability rapidly.

contraindications.warning_title: Do Not Give Food or Fluids
contraindications.warning_message: Victims in hemorrhagic shock or preparing for emergency surgery have compromised airways and high aspiration risk.
contraindications.action_directive: Strictly withhold all water, tea, and oral medicine.

contraindications.warning_title: Do Not Probe or Cut Wound
contraindications.warning_message: Blindly probing, cutting, or attempting to clamp vessels in field conditions worsens hemorrhage and damages nerves.
contraindications.action_directive: Never make surgical incisions or probe bleeding cavities.

protocols.protocol_name: WHO / ERC Airway Obstruction Relief Protocol
protocols.section: Guideline 2.4: Foreign Body Airway Obstruction (FBAO) Management

steps.title: Assess Obstruction Severity
steps.action_instruction: Ask the victim 'Are you choking?'. If the person can cough forcefully or speak, encourage continuous coughing. If they cannot speak, breathe, or cough (silent choking with universal choking sign), intervene immediately.
steps.warning_note: Do not slap the back while victim is coughing effectively.

steps.title: Deliver 5 Firm Back Blows
steps.action_instruction: Stand slightly behind the victim. Support their chest with one hand and lean them forward. Deliver 5 sharp, separate blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your other hand.
steps.warning_note: Check after each blow if the obstruction is dislodged.

steps.title: Perform 5 Abdominal Thrusts (Heimlich Maneuver)
steps.action_instruction: If back blows fail, stand behind the victim, wrap arms around the waist. Make a fist with thumb side against the abdomen just above the navel and below the rib cage. Grasp fist with other hand and pull sharply inward and upward 5 times.
steps.warning_note: For pregnant women or obese individuals, use chest thrusts over the lower breastbone instead of abdominal thrusts.

steps.title: Unconscious Choking Resuscitation
steps.action_instruction: If victim becomes unconscious, support them to the ground. Call 108 emergency ambulance immediately and begin CPR chest compressions at 110 BPM. Each time opening airway, look for the object and sweep out ONLY if clearly visible.
steps.warning_note: Never perform blind finger sweeps; it can push objects deeper into the larynx.

contraindications.warning_message: Sweeping fingers blindly inside a choking victim's mouth can lodge foreign bodies deeper into the trachea.
contraindications.action_directive: Only extract an object if clearly visible and loose.

contraindications.warning_message: Attempting emergency cricothyroidotomy or surgical incisions without surgical training causes fatal vascular injury.
contraindications.action_directive: Never attempt surgical airway creation in the field; continue chest compressions and ventilations.

protocols.protocol_name: WHO / British Burn Association First Aid Protocol
protocols.section: Guideline 7.2: Pre-Hospital Cooling and Burn Wound Management

steps.title: Stop the Burning Process & Remove from Source
steps.action_instruction: Ensure bystander safety. Extinguish flames (Drop and Roll). Disconnect electrical sources or brush off dry chemical powders before irrigation.
steps.warning_note: Do not touch live electrical cables or step into water near downed wires.

steps.title: Cool with Clean Running Water for 20 Minutes
steps.action_instruction: Immediately cool the burn wound with cool running tap water (15–20°C) for a full 20 minutes. Begin cooling within 3 hours of injury.
steps.warning_note: Never use ice, iced water, butter, toothpaste, turmeric, or unverified home remedies; ice causes tissue necrosis.

steps.title: Remove Jewelry and Constrictive Clothing
steps.action_instruction: Gently remove rings, watches, bracelets, and loose clothing before swelling occurs. Do not peel off clothing that is melted or adhered to burned skin.
steps.warning_note: Cut around stuck fabric rather than pulling.

steps.title: Cover with Clean Plastic Cling Film or Sterile Dressing
steps.action_instruction: Cover the cooled burn loosely with layers of clean transparent plastic wrap (cling film) or a sterile non-adherent dressing. Keep the victim warm.
steps.warning_note: Do not wrap cling film tightly around limbs (avoid tourniquet effect as tissues swell).

contraindications.warning_title: Do Not Apply Ice or Freezing Packs
contraindications.warning_message: Ice causes severe vasoconstriction, deepens tissue ischemia, and risks systemic hypothermia.
contraindications.action_directive: Use only cool running tap water for 20 minutes.

contraindications.warning_title: Do Not Apply Ointments, Toothpaste, or Butter
contraindications.warning_message: Greasy substances trap heat within tissues and cause severe microbial wound infections.
contraindications.action_directive: Keep wound clean and covered with dry cling film; do not apply unverified ointments.

protocols.protocol_name: WHO Essential Trauma Care / ATLS Spinal Immobilization
protocols.section: Guideline 5.3: Pre-Hospital Cervical Spine Control & Splinting in Situ

steps.title: Manual In-Line Cervical Spine Stabilization
steps.action_instruction: In high-energy collisions, falls from height, or road traffic accidents, assume spinal cord injury. Kneel at victim's head, hold head firmly with both hands in neutral alignment, and instruct victim not to move.
steps.warning_note: Never tilt, rotate, or bend the neck or spine.

steps.title: Splint Fractured Limbs in Position Found
steps.action_instruction: Immobilize the joint above and below any suspected bone fracture using rigid splints, rolled blankets, or cardboard. Secure with bandages without cutting off distal circulation.
steps.warning_note: Check pulse, skin warmth, and sensation in fingers/toes before and after splinting.

steps.title: Manage Open Fractures (Compound Bone Protrusions)
steps.action_instruction: If bone protrudes through the skin, cover with a sterile, moist dressing. Control surrounding bleeding with direct pressure around the bone.
steps.warning_note: Never attempt to push the protruding bone back inside the skin.

steps.title: Stabilize Impaled Objects in Situ
steps.action_instruction: If a pole, knife, rebar, or glass is embedded in the body, stabilize it with bulky dressings on both sides and tape securely in place.
steps.warning_note: Never remove or pull out an impaled object; it is tamponading torn blood vessels.

contraindications.warning_title: Do Not Push Bones In or Align Fractures
contraindications.warning_message: Attempting field reduction of bone fractures causes severe neurovascular transection, fat embolism, and permanent paralysis.
contraindications.action_directive: Splint the limb exactly in the position found.

contraindications.warning_title: Do Not Pull Out Impaled Objects
contraindications.warning_message: Removing impaled objects unplugs major arteries, causing catastrophic fatal hemorrhage within seconds.
contraindications.action_directive: Stabilize the object with bulky padding in situ.

protocols.section: Guideline 3.1: Hypoxic Cardiac Arrest & Ventilation-First Resuscitation

steps.title: Safe Rescue Without Endangering Rescuer
steps.action_instruction: Reach or throw a flotation device or rope. Do not enter water unless trained. Remove victim horizontally from water to avoid sudden cardiovascular collapse.
steps.warning_note: Rescuer safety is paramount.

steps.title: Deliver 5 Initial Rescue Breaths First
steps.action_instruction: Drowning causes hypoxic arrest. If victim is unresponsive and not breathing, immediately open airway and give 5 rescue breaths before chest compressions.
steps.warning_note: Do not attempt to drain water from lungs with abdominal thrusts.

steps.title: Continue 30:2 CPR at 110 BPM
steps.action_instruction: Perform cycles of 30 chest compressions (110 BPM) followed by 2 rescue breaths. Continue until AED arrives or spontaneous breathing returns.
steps.warning_note: Wipe chest dry before attaching AED pads.

steps.title: Remove Wet Clothes & Rewarm
steps.action_instruction: Strip wet clothing, dry the skin, and cover with dry blankets and insulation from cold ground.
steps.warning_note: Handle gently to prevent triggering ventricular fibrillation in hypothermic hearts.

contraindications.warning_title: Do Not Use Abdominal Thrusts to Drain Water
contraindications.warning_message: Abdominal thrusts cause gastric regurgitation and massive aspiration of stomach contents into the lungs.
contraindications.action_directive: Proceed directly to rescue breathing and chest compressions.
